display.text: Earlier learning makes newly learned information harder to remember.
New learning makes previously learned information harder to remember.
Long-term retention improves when learners actively retrieve information instead of only restudying it.
Learning improves when practice opportunities are distributed across time rather than massed together.
A limited-capacity system temporarily holds and manipulates information for current tasks.
A durable memory system stores information over extended periods.
Recall is better when cues available during retrieval match the context present during learning.
A stimulus or piece of information that helps bring a memory to mind.
Connecting new material to meaningful prior knowledge by adding detail or explanation.
Awareness and regulation of one's own thinking and learning processes.
Applying knowledge or skills learned in one situation to a different situation.
The total mental demand imposed on limited working-memory resources.
